Let me carefully review my analysis one more time.

The task asks about Section 2(b)(2)(C) and whether it "applies to Bob in 2014."

Looking at the statute:

Section 2(b) is the "Definition of head of household."
Section 2(b)(2) is "Determinaton of status."
Section 2(b)(2)(C) states: "a taxpayer shall be considered as married at the close of his taxable year if his spouse (other than a spouse described in subparagraph (B)) died during the taxable year."

The facts:
- Alice and Bob married Feb 3rd, 1992
- Alice died July 9th, 2014
- Year in question: 2014

So in 2014, Bob's spouse (Alice) died during the taxable year (July 9th, 2014). Section 2(b)(2)(C) applies when the spouse dies during the taxable year.

The claim is: "Section 2(b)(2)(C) applies to Bob in 2014."

Since Alice died in 2014, Section 2(b)(2)(C) indeed applies to Bob in 2014. This means the claim is TRUE given the statute and facts.

Therefore, the answer is "Entailment."

I'm confident in this answer. The only risk would be if I misunderstood what "applies" means in this context, but I believe I correctly interpreted it - the statute's provisions are applicable to Bob given the facts.
